programme.title: The Promoter
programme.desc: A con man makes his living by provoking and then betting on gunfights.

programme.title: The Illustrator
programme.desc: Lucas encourages a drunken artist charged with murder to use his talents to identify the true killer.

programme.title: The Silent Knife
programme.desc: Lucas and Mark try to persuade a persecuted young mute to return stolen money.

programme.title: Miss Bertie
programme.desc: A lively old lady arrives in town hot on the trail of a notorious bandit and the reward money for capturing him.

programme.title: Six Years and a Day
programme.desc: A doctor seeks revenge on the man he blames for ruining his practice.

programme.title: Flowers by the Door
programme.desc: Lucas unmasks a killer posing as a door-to-door seed salesman.

programme.title: Long Trek
programme.desc: Lucas and Marshall Torrance run into trouble while transporting a captured killer back to face trial.

programme.title: The Actress
programme.desc: A deathbed request from an old friend sends Lucas to a neighboring town in search of the man's sweetheart.

programme.title: Face of Yesterday
programme.desc: Lucas thinks he has seen a ghost when a man, eerily similar to a man he killed, challenges him to a gunfight.

programme.title: The Wyoming Story: Part 1
programme.desc: Lucas agrees to take a job as an undercover agent and goes to investigate rumors of the sales of arms to renegade Indians. His life is endangered by the town drunk who stumbles onto his true identity.

programme.title: The Wyoming Story: Part 2
programme.desc: While Lucas is in Wyoming on the trail of a gang illegally selling weapons to the Indians, Mark stays with Miss Milly, where he suffers from loneliness and doubt with his father gone for 2 months.

programme.title: Closer Than a Brother
programme.desc: Lucas looks for answers when recovering alcoholic Micah Torrence returns to the bottle and turns in his badge.

programme.title: The Lost Treasure of Canyon Town
programme.desc: Lucas, Mark and Micah tangle with the Newman family and learn the secret of a town's 20-year-old mystery.

programme.title: Dark Day at North Fork
programme.desc: Blinded in an explosion, Lucas fights despair as he prepares for a meeting with a gun-toting enemy.

programme.title: The Prisoner
programme.desc: A deranged ex-prisoner of war, cruelly abused in a Northern army prison, captures Lucas, locks him in a cage and vows to make him suffer for his part in the Civil War.

programme.title: Assault
programme.desc: A traveling salesman can't talk his way out of an assault charge.

programme.title: Short Rope for a Tall Man
programme.desc: Lucas is threatened with hanging by a lynch party when some horses he has purchased in a neighboring town turn out to be stolen.

programme.title: The Clarence Bibs Story
programme.desc: A janitor-turned-gunfighter's reputation hangs on one lucky shot and a lot of gall. The handyman finds himself in trouble when he accidentally kills another gunfighter.

programme.title: The Score Is Even
programme.desc: Lucas tries to get help when he is shot after witnessing a murder.

programme.title: The Mescalaro Curse
programme.desc: After being foreman of a jury that convicted an Apache, Lucas is marked for death. Now, he must discover who is behind the curse.

programme.title: Stopover
programme.desc: Lucas allows some snowed-in stagecoach passengers to stay with him until the roads are passable. Trouble brews when the whisky salesman and gunfighter fall for the same woman.

programme.title: The Lonesome Bride
programme.desc: Two pranksters write away for a mail-order bride, using Lucas's name.

programme.title: Death Trap
programme.desc: Lucas recognizes Dr. Battle as an ex-gunslinger with whom he once fought. He helps with a dying man, but Lucas and the doctor have unresolved anger.

programme.title: The Queue
programme.desc: A Chinese man and his son fight prejudice as they try to open a laundry in North Fork.

programme.title: The Vaqueros
programme.desc: While Lucas and Mark are traveling across the Mexican desert they encounter a trio of Mexican bandits who demand payment to cross "their" desert.

programme.title: First Wages
programme.desc: Mark takes a job as a stable boy against his father's wishes.

programme.title: Sheer Terror
programme.desc: Mark and Milly are held hostage in her general store when two gunmen attempt a daring robbery.

programme.title: The Stand-In
programme.desc: Two prison wagon drivers stop at the McCain ranch looking for whiskey. Lucas turns them down because they are escorting a murderer, to be hanged in Yuma.

programme.title: The Journey Back
programme.desc: Mark goes to work for Will Temple, a badly scarred, very mysterious rancher.

programme.title: The Decision
programme.desc: Corey Hazlett insists he's innocent of murder, despite Lucas's eyewitness testimony.

programme.title: Knight Errant
programme.desc: Lucas tries to dissuade a latter-day knight from rushing into battle.

programme.title: Serrania de le Macerena
programme.desc: In the middle of Colombia, lies an ancient, unique and little explored outcrop of sandstone; the Serrania de la Macarena. It forms part of the country's first ever national park - made up of lush jungle, shrubland and savannah, isolated peaks, winding rivers and spectacular waterfalls - where more than 15 million specimens were collected during early studies of the area. Called the 'treasure of the world', scientists believe it is a hugely important bank of biological diversity.

programme.title: May
programme.desc: While we celebrate may day, the coming of summer, there are many changes going on in the world. As snows finally melt in the mountains of Europe, chamois lambs have the chance to test out their climbing skills and explore their vertical home, watching all the time for eagles, their main predators. On the vast plains of the Russian the weird looking saiga antelope have their calves, while Florida enters its fire season and even the everglades can burn

programme.title: These Birds Are Made For Walking
programme.desc: Few things are more wondrous than the gift of flight, but some birds have chosen to give it up - the question is, why? Whether it's to save energy, tap into new food resources or invest in other skills, they all have their reasons. But one thing's for sure: it doesn't make flightless birds any less weird and wonderful. There are 60 species of bird that have given up the gift of flight, but they are not all related. Each have taken their own evolutionary path.

programme.title: Coasts - Rolling with the Waves
programme.desc: We love our coasts, and so do animals! The corridor of water where the open ocean transitions into coastal habitat is known as the surf zone. The churning forces of the waves clashing with the land make these some of the most food-rich waters on Earth. Nutrients are both washed off the coast from rain and rivers, but also pushed up from the depths thanks to waves and currents.

programme.title: Extinction! Going, going, gone!
programme.desc: Extinction, a daunting and confusing word. A force of nature, that sees the end of species, but also heralds the birth of others. Right now the extinction rate could be as much as 10,000 times faster than it should be. 20% of fish, a fifth of all reptiles and a quarter of mammals face extinction. If we are to do anything to stem the tide of extinction we must understand the lifestyles of those in danger.

programme.title: Caribbean
programme.desc: The Caribbean has been shaped by millions of years of unstoppable volcanic forces and ferocious hurricanes, creating a network of 7,000 islands, each one more unique than the next. From islets only a few miles long to landmasses with towering peaks, the habitats of this tropical paradise range from lush rainforests hiding untold species to multi-coloured coral reefs teeming with marine life.

programme.title: Deadly Bite
programme.desc: Many animals have evolved chemicals to enhance their chance of survival: some scorpions literally drug their potential mates, others use their poisons to defend or kill. The world of venoms and poisons, the apparatus designed to deliver the payload and the strategies that animals employ to use them most effectively is a rich and varied example of natural selection and evolution in action.

programme.title: Vancouver
programme.desc: Nestled alongside Canada's south west coast, Vancouver Island is home to the richest Pacific wildlife. Sea lions and killer whales are among the marine predators enjoying the abundant seafood in the surrounding waters, while black bears, marmots and beavers enjoy the rich pickings on land. But each fall, the islands inhabitants must adapt and prepare to face the coming winter. Some will leave, among them humpback whales and turkey vultures who migrate to warmer climes.

programme.title: A life for animals
programme.desc: Hannah runs a health check on two female cheetahs with veterinarian Maaike. She then goes into the wilderness with Naankuse founder Marlice. Together they go in search of the elephant Apollo, which was resettled in the sanctuary. The former "problem" elephant now leads a peaceful life here.

programme.title: Seasons Of The Otter
programme.desc: One of the most loves animals, famed for its playful nature and incredible underwater agility. Yet most of the life of the otter goes unseen. Following the first year in the life of a young otter family, we'll reveal the secrets of the otter's world. Otter life is often a challenge, and especially so for a young family trying to make it through winter. Two pups were born last spring, and as they approach their first birthdays the time with their mother is coming to its end.

programme.title: Moose Mayhem
programme.desc: This unique arctic city is home over 2000 moose! And these notorious animals are running riot... Crossing busy highways, giving birth in backyards, and even doing battle, right here in suburbia! But life on the streets is fraught with danger...and in this expanding city, more highways mean more moose deaths. But the people of Anchorage are on a mission, to protect the most iconic animal in this Wild City.

programme.title: Maui and Moloka''
programme.desc: In episode two we take a look at Maui and Moloka'i. In the middle of the archipelago they form the heart of Hawaii. The second largest island of Hawai'i - Maui - is a true paradise for surfers. Archie Kalepa was one of the first big wave surfers and is still chasing the thrill today. The ukulele represents the sound of the islands like no other instrument. Eric Devine has been building the plucked string instrument for 20 years. In Kula he goes in search of the perfect wood.

programme.title: Elephant 911/North Bengal
programme.desc: Elephant human conflict has been going on in India for decades. Only now it has increased because of the shrinking forests and the expanding human habitation. North Bengal with it's fragmented habitat of tea gardens, human habitation and paddy fields is a hot bed of conflict. We follow an elephant flying squad which is responsible for keeping the elephants away from these human dominated landscapes.

programme.title: Sexy Beasts
programme.desc: Driven by surging hormones, every creature on the planet, big or small, will do whatever it takes to find and secure a mate. For some this will take the fight of their lives, while others must preen, prance and party their way to success. From one night stands and group sex to lifelong love and unbreakable bonds, when it comes to finding a mate the animal kingdom has it all. The need to breed manifests itself in all sorts of wonderful antics, displays and behaviours.

programme.title: Life at the Extremes
programme.desc: In nature, competition for territory is so extreme that some animals have resorted to living in incredible hostile conditions. From brutal cold, to extreme heat, from the ocean depths, to the driest of deserts, this episode showcases some incredible survival stories in the world's most inhospitable environments.

programme.title: The Great Barrier Reef
programme.desc: One of Australia's most remarkable natural gifts. The Great Barrier Reef in all it's breath-taking beauty. It is the world's largest coral reef, acknowledged as one of the seven wonders of the natural world, and viewed from a greater distance it's easy to understand why. It is larger than the Great Wall of China and the only living thing on earth visible from space. The Great Barrier Reef supports a vast array of life forms.

programme.title: Arctic
programme.desc: The Arctic is alive with a fascinating assortment of wildlife and species that are unique to this Polar environment. Most of are rarely or never seen outside the Arctic Circle. They live and thrive in a hostile environment of ice, polar desert, wind-swept open tundra, ancient glacial formations, sub zero sea temperatures and an incredible variety of geographical topo-graphy from open plain and valleys to mountainous peaks and deep water fiords.

programme.title: American Praire
programme.desc: Prairies are a temperate grassland. Vast great plains, extremely hot in summer and cold in winter. Moderate rainfall, and a composition of grasses, herbs and shrubs, rather than trees characterise these plains. Most of North America was a vast prairie before European settlement and agriculture radically altered the environment.

programme.title: Jungle of Asia
programme.desc: Some of the most beautiful rainforest, jungle landscape and wildlife are in Asia. The rainforests of Asia stretch from India and Burma in the west to Malaysia and the islands of Java and Borneo in the east. The Great teak forests and Jungles in Asia have long been under threat from intensive logging and industrial farming of cash crops. Slash and burn agriculture has also taken a heavy toll on the eco-structure and environment. Bangladesh has the largest mangrove forests in the world.

programme.title: Egypt
programme.desc: 96% of Egypt's lands are sun-blistered desert. Rock and sand dominate this country, creating a beautiful but hostile environment. Yet it was home to the Worlds greatest ancient civilisation, which flourished for millennia and still captivates us today. These harsh lands also hold amazing animals that can survive and even thrive, able to cope with and profit from the searing temperatures and lack of moisture.

programme.title: Lion - Africa's Super Power
programme.desc: The endless plains of East Africa is a paradise for lions. The most social of all cats, lions form prides that are unlike any other animals. Together, they'll hunt, raise their young and defend their territory. With such a close family and plentiful home, the pride welcomes new babies every year. But new children introduces new dangers.

programme.title: Meet the Marsupials
programme.desc: Few countries have a more iconic representative in the animal kingdom than Australia and the marsupial. Once marsupials were found across the planet, but over time they found their way to the outback, leaving Australia as an ark carrying the future of pouch mammals. As varied as they are unusual, marsupials are a weird and wonderful mob of animals who carry their young in a pouch.

programme.title: Falklands
programme.desc: The Falkland Islands' pristine coastlines and bountiful seas offer a lifeline and breeding centre for millions of penguins each year. Though while some find sanctuary on dry land, there's a daily battle to survive in the waters which surround these wild and rocky shores.

programme.title: Return of the Sharks
programme.desc: In the aftermath of Cape Towns biggest storm in 2 decades, there's a whole lot of work to be done at the Two Oceans Aquarium! The pressure builds as nine Ragged-Toothed Sharks are on their way from East London for their introduction to the new, highly anticipated predator exhibit. Join the team in one last push to complete the giant tank in time for its incoming residents and see the experience the culmination of a year of hard work coming together, at the Two Oceans Aquarium!

programme.title: Animals of the Bible
programme.desc: The bible is one of the most famous texts on earth. But it doesn't just concern humans, it also mentions animals - and some of these are probably not what you'd expect. We've all heard of the ox and the ass, the donkey that carried Mary, but did you know gazelles are mentioned in the bible? Or that great whales, cunning leopards and even the energetic hyrax feature?

programme.title: Bears Behaving Badly
programme.desc: Anchorage is home to hundreds of black bears. And it's these black bears, that are patrolling the city. With their brains, their brawn and their cunning, these bears have mastered life in this urban jungle. When Spring arrives the bears hit the city as it's time to start eating. And these bears have found a source of food that is much easier to catch than a slippery salmon - it's trash. And it is everywhere. The city's bins and dumpsters have become the perfect bear restaurant.

programme.title: The Green Corridors
programme.desc: The tropical rainforests of Costa Rica provide an invaluable habitat to several emblematic species, such as jaguars, tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, spider monkeys, the very rear green macaw, amongst many others. Most of them are protected in national parks, reserves and wildlife refuges. However, the long-term survival of these ecosystems and of their biodiversity rely on the success of connecting wildlife populations throughout the country.

programme.title: Migrations - Herds on the Move
programme.desc: Whether driven by the search for food or the simple will to survive, great herd migrations are some of the most spectacular events of the natural world.

programme.title: Longevity
programme.desc: Aldabra Tortoise, Matriarch Elephants, Kittiwakes, Honey Bees, Hydra, Lions In this episode of Aging in the Wild, we explore the physiological secrets and factors that determine life expectancy in various animal species. From the seventy-year-old elephant to the quasi-immortal hydra, and the more than a hundred-year-old tortoise, we explore life expectancy, longevity and senescence. Can we distinguish between the effects of the environment and the internal adaptations that lead to longevity?

programme.title: Power & Dominance
programme.desc: Bighorn Sheep, Elk, Male Elephants, Marmots, Baboons, Rhinos Observing two massive elk clashing their antlers is to witness a true demonstration of power. For other species, such as the European marmot, remaining in power is a matter of collaborating with family and community. Are these animals forced to give up their hard-won social status as they age? Through this lens, we take a deep and entertaining look at the challenges faced by those in power ... and what it takes to stay there.

programme.title: Nuts About Squirrels
programme.desc: Even in our most urban settings, pretty much all of us know squirrels. They can be divisive charac-ters; some people adore them, offering them food, while others see them as glorified rats. But we can all agree that these are speedy, quirky, and exceptional characters. They also go crazy for nuts. They've conquered most of the globe, from icy tundra to the hottest deserts, developing ingen-ious life skills along the way, from stashing nuts to fighting snakes.

programme.title: Lions Rule
programme.desc: The Lion, Africa's ultimate predator. An essay in power and agility, famed for the cut-throat gang and the killer instinct. Lions are known as the kings of the jungle yet their homeland is an open grassland rather than rainforest. In the African plains prey-rich real estate can be hard to come by, and lions work together to ensure no one claims their territory and usurps their crown.

programme.title: Reproduction
programme.desc: Lions, Chimpanzees, Turtles, Roe Deer, Gannets Reproduction is not only a concern of the young and restless: this episode of Aging in the Wild brings a light-hearted look at the issue of sexuality and camaraderie in older animals. We illustrate, for example, the link between the age of an elephant and its reproductive success. What are the reproductive benefits of these animals as they grow older?

programme.title: Sri Lanka: Monsoon Island
programme.desc: Lying like a teardrop in the Indian Ocean, Sri Lanka is an island that defies convention. Poised just six degrees above the equator, it's less than 75,000 km sq in size. But it has enough wildlife to rival a continent, and it's all down to its complicated climate and geography.

programme.title: Bald Eagle Rescue
programme.desc: In Anchorage, one bird rules the roost...the Bald Eagle. Expert hunters, they are perfectly adapted to life in tough arctic conditions, but in Anchorage, the secret to their survival... is trash. Every day, hundreds of bald eagles gather at the city dump, dodging trucks, machinery, and even pyrotechnics, in search of an easy meal. But this city life also brings constant danger, for the eagles themselves, and also for the human residents.

programme.title: City Lynx
programme.desc: One of Alaska's most secretive and efficient predators, Lynx are usually highly elusive... but in Anchorage, houses are being built in the Lynx's territory, forcing these usually shy big cats, to find new ways to survive on the streets. As this urban jungle continues to expand into the wilderness, encounters between people and wild Lynx are on the rise. In this wild city, can people live side by side with Alaska's deadliest big cat?

programme.title: Migrations - Frequent Flyers
programme.desc: Migration is one of the most remarkable phenomena of the natural world, and perhaps the most impressive migrants of all travel on the wing.

programme.title: Owls - Masters of the Night
programme.desc: Owls are mysterious creatures, living in a twilight world that we can rarely visit. Many cultures, including the Romans, Mayans and Aztecs, saw owls as something to fear, symbols of bad luck and impending doom. In reality owls are highly resourceful birds that have carved out a niche and a unique way to live. They range in size from smaller than a pigeon to as large as an eagle. They've colonised terrains from tundra to rainforest.

programme.title: Turkey
programme.desc: Turkey sits on a jumbled collection of tectonic plates, whose collisions have created a tortuous landscape. In fact 80% of Turkeys terrain is rough, broken and mountainous. Mountain ranges both collect and block weather systems, affecting the climate across the country and producing huge contrasts between and within differing habitats.

programme.title: Wild Uruguay
programme.desc: Uruguay's biodiversity is surprisingly greater than one would expect. We will find out why as we embark on a journey through its ecosystems and landscapes to discover its fauna. Today we know that Uruguay is more than just the outermost edge of the Pampas, as the country holds a range of ecosystems. Within its borders, species of the Pampas come face to face with species of the Atlantic Forest, the Misiones rainforest, and the Chaco forest, giving rise to unexpected encounters.

programme.title: The Enchanted Forest
programme.desc: To spend a day in the forest, from dawn to dusk, is to bathe in nature. There's enchantment at every turn. Throughout the day the cast of characters in the forest changes, from foraging bears to playing fox cubs, dashing hummingbirds and dancing butterflies. But it's as twilight descends, that the most enchanting side of the forest is revealed. Time to watch a firework display curtesy of fireflies. They are the real magicians of the enchanted forest.

programme.title: Open Ocean
programme.desc: It might look uniform from the air, as we fly over it, but the oceans are deep and varied. The underwater landscape is made up of continental shelves, volcanoes, mountains, valleys, trenches and large, flat plains similar to the landscape on land only on a much larger scale. Ocean habitats come in all forms. Under water creatures make homes wherever survival is assured.

programme.title: Westlands
programme.desc: Large areas of water, broken up by small islands. Massive vegetation. Swamps, wetlands, marshes, bogs and fens are found all over the world, generally in more temperate regions where there is fast vegetation growth. Many of the larger animals that inhabit swamps and wetlands have a fish-based diet. LARGE CRABS dwell in the salt-water swamps, along with SNAPPING TURTLES and even CROCODILES AND ALLIGATORS. LIZARDS AND AMPHIBIANS live in and around the water's edge.

programme.title: Desert
programme.desc: Deserts - dry, arid landscapes, environments of intense sun, heat and very little rain. The desert is extreme. An extre-me climate and an extreme environment where wild life has had to adapt to survive. Many of the animals that live in deserts have adopted a nocturnal lifestyle, surfacing only at night when it is cooler.

programme.title: Master of the Sky
programme.desc: The masters of the sky are the winged predators of the aerial world. Whether swooping from altitude at phenomenal speed to strike an unsuspecting target from above, flicking and darting between trees in a lethal tail chase, or ghos-ting silently through the night in pursuit of prey, they excite our admiration and inspire awe in equal measure. All are superbly adapted to hunting and masters of their position at the top of the food chain.

programme.title: Cost of Progress
programme.desc: The natural world is in crisis. For years humanity has exploited the planet's resources, and the creatures that live here. Growth and innovation can be a marvelous thing, but at what cost to our one and only planet? When we continue to push ahead blindly, it's more often than not Mother Nature that pays the price. Now it is time for us to rally - to take heed and start to turn back the tide. It's time for us to recognize our part in this crisis and redress the balance of the cost of progress.

programme.title: Life Below Zero
programme.desc: Over the last million years, our planet suffered a series of major ice-ages. Much of the northern hemisphere was covered in ice sheets several kilometres thick and creatures had no choice but to adapt or die. Over time, temperatures rose, causing these glaciers to retreat, however, in certain parts of Europe the ice-age never left. For many creatures, the struggle to survive 'a life below zero' continues.

programme.title: Baked Alaska
programme.desc: This city spends most of the year encased in ice...but when summer hits, Anchorage bursts into life. Animals and plants living this far north have been forced to adapt, working faster to make the most of the short season, but these animals built to withstand Alaska's extreme winters, often struggle in Anchorage's summer heat! Temperatures can be surprisingly high, with average July highs of 26 degrees C. 300,000 people live alongside these wild animals in the ever growing city of Anchorage.

programme.title: Creepy Crawlies - Army
programme.desc: Few creatures have the complex levels of regimented society as the social insects; these creatures understand that the strength of the individual is nothing compared with the combined power of the group. Creepy crawlies can form armies to help them build elaborate homes, raise their young and hunt their prey. These incredible communities both plagues our nightmares and fuels our imaginations. Society is considered the realm of higher beings, but hidden amongst the foliage, an army is rising.

programme.title: Wisdom
programme.desc: Grizzly Bears, Orcas, Elephants, Wolves, Olive Baboons In many human cultures, elders play a vital role in the well-being of communities and are responsible for passing down knowledge and culture. Is it any wonder to find that the orca, the elephant, and the wolf, have been found to transmit their respective cultures to the younger generations? Young animals learn by observing their elders.

programme.title: Top of the South/ Te Tau Ihu
programme.desc: The top of New Zealand's South Island is a landscape of two halves. To the West, one of the longest natural sandbars on the planet curves protectively around Golden Bay. To the East, mountains sink into the sea, their drowned river valleys forming the Marlborough Sounds. Turbulent currents connect them, both treacherous and full of riches.

programme.title: Urban Warrirors
programme.desc: As human populations grow, so does our footprint, and more of the natural world is gradually paved over, displacing animals from their natural homes. It presents a staggering number of difficulties for those creatures that find themselves cut off from their natural habitat, but there is a growing band of urban warriors stepping up to the challenge. City life for some means living on the breadline, while others discover a land of opportunity - a new concrete frontier.

programme.title: Muaūpoko /Otago Peninsula
programme.desc: On the doorstep of one of the country's biggest cities, Muaūpoko /Otago Peninsula provides a breeding refuge for birds and marine mammals. Northern royal albatrosses return here every year to raise their chicks at the world's only mainland colony. On sheltered beaches around the Peninsula, once hunted from these shores, New Zealand sea lions are returning to form a breeding colony after an absence of centuries.

programme.title: Mother's Day
programme.desc: Being a wild mum is one of the toughest jobs on earth. From the second a mother gives birth, everything changes. No longer footloose and fancy free, they find themselves completely responsible for tiny, delicate little lives - lives that would be helpless without them. For some, being a mother comes naturally, whilst for others it will take a little practoce. But while the responsibility is immense, being a mum is also incredible.

programme.title: Easter The Start of Something Big
programme.desc: Easter, not just a chocolate feast loved by children. One of the biggest events in the religious calendar, celebrated by millions and steeped in customs and traditions. And for all its different meanings there are some key characters we associate with the holiday: chicks, bunnies and lambs have become integral to our celebrations. How have these animals become a part of Easter tradition? There are many twists and turns in the story, but without a doubt this is the start of something big!

programme.title: Episode 001
programme.desc: Owls - with their huge eyes, flat faces and distinctive hoot - they are truly iconic!creatures. But how much do we really know about these mysterious nocturnal birds? We're about to find out as we follow the fate of new born baby owls as they grow up and learn to fly.

programme.title: Hidden Spain
programme.desc: Spain is found at the crossroads between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, resulting in diverse landscapes, ancient cultures and magnificent wildlife.

programme.title: Kaua''i
programme.desc: In epsiode one we take a look at Kaua'i - the oldest island in the archipelago. Kaua'i's isolation for thousands of years led to an increased rate of evolution. In a relatively short time, new species are formed here, many animals and plants can only be found here. But they are in danger. On the shield volcano Waiʻaleʻale - the rainiest place on earth, scientists like Lukas Behnke are fighting for the preservation of endangered native animals and plants.

programme.title: Hunters of the Forest
programme.desc: Forests are dark, shady habitats, realms of shadows perfect for predators to lurk. The dense plant growth facilitates a wealth of prey species, and cunning predators of all shapes and sizes have adapted to exploit every niche. Whether crawling on the forest floor, gliding through the trees or stalking the shadows in between, hunters have mastered the terrain in every type of forest imagina-ble.

programme.title: June
programme.desc: It's chaos in the Northern hemisphere, our bird feeders are busy as parents work around the clock to raise their young. There's a baby boom, and young foxes, even in our city centres, leave their dens to explore. Its winter in the south though, cold times for guanacos on the slopes of the Andes. And dry times for elephants in Botswana. They migrate north to the life-giving waters of the Chobe River

programme.title: Nature's Oddballs - Creatures of the Night
programme.desc: hile we sleep comfortably in our beds, one of the most spectacular groups of animals go to work - prepare to meet the creatures of the night!

programme.title: Te Moananui a Toi/ The Hauraki Gulf
programme.desc: Te Moananui a Toi/ The Hauraki Gulf lies on the doorstep of New Zealand's largest city. Every summer millions of visitors from the tropics converge here, all lured by a unique seasonal smorgasbord. Giant oceanic manta rays, rarely filmed in these waters, glide into the gulf. Bryde's whales are also primed for the feasting season, alongside common dolphins, and bronze whaler sharks. In the sky above rare black petrels stalk the dolphins to survive.

programme.title: My Fair Bagel
programme.desc: Action Bronson makes his mighty return to Auckland, introducing Meyhem to his favourite burger truck.

programme.title: New Orleans D.I.Y
programme.desc: Rick introduces us to DIY culture in New Orleans: a city on the mend.

programme.title: Let There Be Light
programme.desc: It's crunch time as interns prepare presentations and Hatch Panama brings lights & leaders to the jungle.

programme.title: The Return

programme.title: Japan, Here We Come

programme.title: Stirring the Pot
programme.desc: L 2 Chainz tastes THC butter from a $15K machine and treats from a $400 home edible kit.

programme.title: Tex Mex
programme.desc: 2 Chainz hits up Dallas to study the wide world of Tex Mex cuisine.

programme.title: Route 66
programme.desc: Rick and co-pilot Frank Gerwer check out the roadkill on what's left of Route 66.

programme.title: Nuclear Waste
programme.desc: Rick explores doomsday paranoia in the nuclear relics of the Pacific Northwest.

programme.title: Detroit Dilemma
programme.desc: Rick finds out you can't believe the hype - good or bad - about the Motor City.

programme.title: Pioneers or Colonists
programme.desc: Interns challenge the purpose of their new community are they doing more harm than good?

programme.title: Entertaining Jungle-Style
programme.desc: Jimmy shows off his jungle playground, but is challenged by interns worried about their environmental impact.

programme.title: The Hammer Falls Hardest Here
programme.desc: Hitler's fortress Europe begins to crumble with Nazi occupying forces fall back on every front. The US Army Air Force grows to become the biggest armada the world has ever seen, gaining the air superiority needed to ensure complete victory.

programme.title: Prelude to War
programme.desc: The surrender at Reims ended the major phase of the European Theater of WWII. The film dissolves from the surrender to Hitler in his early years of power, follows the rise of Nazism through the Munich Pact, the attack on Poland, the fall of France, and the Battle of Britain.

programme.title: Hitler's Death Army - Part II: Death and Decline
programme.desc: With recolorized archives, this episode explores the final year of Hitler's infamous division. From recruitment and indoctrination to their last missions, we uncover who these men were-and how they became perpetrators of mass murder. Following their brutal combat and crimes against humanity, we confront the chaos, ideology, and horror that defined the Das Reich's final descent.

programme.title: Conquering the Sky
programme.desc: When humans took to the skies, they brought war with them. This episode traces aerial combat from WWI dogfights to bombers, jets, and drones. Exploring how air power evolved into one of the deadliest forces in warfare, it highlights the relentless drive to fly faster, strike harder, and control the skies-forever changing the face of battle from above.

programme.title: The Night of the Long Knives: Hitler's Rise to Power
programme.desc: The Night of the Long Knives is considered the first act of horror committed by the Nazis. What happened in Germany, and in Hitler's rise to power, that led to this purge in 1934? Caught between the conservative tendency and the revolutionary aspirations that were dividing the country, the Chancellor had a choice. To calm the rumors of a military coup against him, Hitler sent a clear message.

programme.title: By Night & By Day
programme.desc: Tokyo's firebombing proved deadly-wood and paper homes made cities burn fast. The B-29 bomber and napalm upped the carnage. In Europe, USAAF and RAF bombed day and night. New tech like bunker busters and bouncing bombs made targets harder to hide. The bomber was now war's most fearsome force.

programme.title: Memories of WWII
programme.desc: Amateur filmmakers in Normandy secretly documented daily life between 1939-1945, risking arrest under Nazi rule. Preserved for decades, their footage reveals war's darkest hours-shortages, fear, and ruins-yet also family bonds, joy, and hope. This documentary offers an extraordinary civilian perspective, intertwining anonymous lives with the unfolding tragedy and liberation of WWII.

programme.title: D-Day 1944, 101st & 82nd Airborne, Victory's Angels
programme.desc: June 5th, 1944, 9:30 PM. 13,348 men from two American parachute divisions, the 82nd and the 101st Airborne in nearly 1,000 aircraft will take off to Normandy. Until then, no one had launched an airborne operation of this scale. The Allied staff is expecting huge losses! Some forecasts predict 75% of the paratroopers will fall in combat. They must open the way to the troops landing on Utah Beach.

programme.title: Night Jump
programme.desc: In mid-August 1944, the Allies launched 'Operation Anvil' to increase pressure on German troops after the Normandy landings. The 517th Airborne was tasked with preventing enemy tanks from reaching the beachhead. This episode recounts the story of three American sergeants and a British major who jumped into enemy territory, successfully completed their mission, and survived to tell the tale.

programme.title: Stalingrad
programme.desc: After the failure to take both Moscow and Leningrad, Hitler sets his sights on the oil fields in the Caucasus. If captured, the Red Army will lose 70-90% of all its oil resources. Therefore, the famous city on the Volga, Stalingrad, must be 'held at all costs.' The German General Staff thinks taking the city will be a matter of a few weeks, but events steadily turn against the Germans.

programme.title: WWII War Diaries: 1941
programme.desc: In this third film of the series, '1941', see how Adolf Hitler increased the Nazi stranglehold on Europe, while Winston Churchill inspired the people of Britain to stand together as the nightly Luftwaffe bombing raids were extended to include the nation's vital ports, as well as the capital, London.

programme.title: Private Lopez
programme.desc: Meet Jose Lopez, a man who can forage chicken from deserted farms and cook it, a la Mexican, but also a fighting man. Watch him prove himself, carrying weapons and ammunition through enemy fire, firing his machine gun with deadly accuracy, holding off almost singlehandedly a deadly attack. Watch this Laredo, Texas, born-and-bred soldier earn the nation's highest award and the nickname, 'Tex'.

programme.title: The Battle for Germany
programme.desc: Germany is retreating on all fronts and suffering defeat after defeat. The breach of Germany's pre-War borders now seems inevitable. Desperate, Hitler orders all males between the ages of 16 and 70 to enlist and fight for the fatherland. Nazi ideologues put faith in victory and the Nazis seem to vanquish and suppress all forms of doubt and resistance in the last months of the Reich.

programme.title: The Battle of Midway and Beyond: April-June 1942
programme.desc: The American Navy got back on course after Pearl Harbour, and in the four-day Battle for the Coral Sea, they claimed victory, before defeating Japan again in the decisive Battle of Midway. Elsewhere the Luftwaffe targeted more British cities.

programme.title: El Alamein to Stalingrad: July-September 1942
programme.desc: Hitler's 'Desert Fox', Rommel advanced at El Alamein, but with the arrival of British General, Bernard Montgomery, to lead the Eighth Army in North Africa, the wind of change was about to blow.

programme.title: Newsreel Reports on Preparation for D-Day
programme.desc: Prefabricated concrete barges are manufactured in preparation for D Day. U.S. troops storm a beach in a practice landing assault. How harbor facilities made in England were used in the Normandy invasion. A storm damages the harbor but unloading continues.

programme.title: First Aid and the Taking of Cherbourg
programme.desc: The processing of plasma and penicillin. Troops in Normandy receive medical care. Naval guns bombard Cherbourg. The 8th and 9th Air Forces bomb communication lines. British troops take Caen. Shows Gen. Montgomery.

programme.title: Part 10 - Scorched Earth
programme.desc: With the fall of Nazi Germany, the focus shifts to the Pacific, where Japan continues to resist fiercely. This episode covers the brutal island campaigns, kamikaze attacks, and the increasingly destructive U.S. bombing campaigns. Japan's refusal to surrender prompts the U.S. to deploy a new and terrifying weapon: the atomic bomb.

programme.title: The Famous Third Army
programme.desc: A historical record of the 281 days of the 3rd army offensive through France, Belgium and Germany, with air support from the 19th tactical air command.

programme.title: Nazi Concentration Camps
programme.desc: This film is the official documentary report compiled from over 80,000 feet of film shot by Allied military photographers in the German concentration camps immediately after liberation. The footage is a camp-by-camp record taken in order to provide lasting objective proof of the horrors the liberators witnessed. Some emphasis is also placed on the humanitarian work done in camps by the liberators.

programme.title: Part Two
programme.desc: By 1942, Soviet industry-rebuilt in the east-fueled the Red Army with mass-produced tanks, planes, and weapons, reversing the tide at Stalingrad. But while the war economy thrived, civilians starved under famine and rationing. With Allied aid and relentless sacrifice, the USSR rose as an industrial giant-at a staggering human cost.

programme.title: The Reason Why
programme.desc: The first program looks at the reasons behind the war, and why Britain allied itself against Imperial Russia.

programme.title: Blitzed: Nazis on Drugs
programme.desc: In 1938 a drug called Pervitin was created in Nazi Germany. This drug was distributed to German soldiers during the course of WW2 and Hitler was no exception to these drug highs receiving drug cocktails from his personal physical Theodor Morell. This film explores the use of drugs in WW2 and looks at the potential effects that drugs could have had on Hitler, soldiers and the war itself.

programme.title: The Normandy Campaign
programme.desc: From the hedgerows of Normandy to the liberation of Paris, this episode retraces the 100 critical days after D-Day. Witness the fierce battles, the resilience of soldiers, and the toll on civilians as the Allies push through German defenses, paving the way for Europe's liberation and altering the course of World War II.

programme.title: WWII War Diaries: 1940
programme.desc: In '1940,' we follow Hitler's trail of occupation into Denmark and Norway, the invasion of Belgium and France & the Miracle Of Dunkirk where Churchill initiated Operation Dynamo to rescue the thousands of BEF that were stranded & helpless on the beaches under relentless Nazi attack. See how Hitler's Blitzkrieg ripped through France and how the British survive The Blitz & win the Battle Of Britain.

programme.title: The Siege of Leningrad
programme.desc: Leningrad, a vital and large Baltic sea port, is facing the entire weight of Army Group North. The Soviets have no reserves to spare as the Battle of Moscow is about to begin. Wilhelm von Leeb's Army Group North fails to take Leningrad, but begins a horrible siege that will last 872 days, in which over a million civilians will die of starvation and disease.

programme.title: Ma Horner
programme.desc: This is the story of a young apple-cheeked Sergeant nick-named 'Ma' by his men because of his protective nature toward their scouting unit. It is also the tale of Pat Cassidy, a looter of watches and wine and a member of Horner's unit. How these two opposites combine their talents to single-handedly capture a German-held land mine control center, makes a spellbinding, action-packed episode.

programme.title: The Atom Strikes
programme.desc: First experimental blast set off in New Mexico; bombing and devastation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. and devastation of Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

programme.title: Hitler: A Strategy of Failure
programme.desc: Adolf Hitler, considered himself to be the world's greatest military strategist - superior even to Napoleon Bonaparte - and early Blitzkrieg successes could be said to easily confirm this assertion. So why did the Nazis lose the war? Hitler also made colossal strategic military blunders: Dunkirk, Operation Barbarossa and many others that were ultimately a strategy of failure.

programme.title: The Reason Why
programme.desc: The first program looks at the reasons behind the war, and why Britain allied itself against Imperial Russia.

programme.title: Death in the Bunker
programme.desc: Death In The Bunker: The True Story of Hitler's Downfall examines the final 10 days in the Berlin Führerbunker deep below the Chancellery of the Reich. Includes interviews with Hitler's confidants and eyewitnesses including Hitler's Secretary Traudl Junge who after typing out Hitler's will, remained in the bunker until his death. Learn firsthand what happened in the bunker right to the very end.

programme.title: Big Picture: The Army Medical Corps
programme.desc: Graphically shown here is the treatment given our wounded in battle. We see the care a man receives from medics all along the line; from the time the wounded soldier calls 'Medic' until he is released for duty. The Medical Corps is saving more lives than in any other time of combat. Lieutenant Colonel S. J. Newsom of San Diego, California tells the story in an interview with Captain Zimmerman.

programme.title: Partners, Plans, and Provisions
programme.desc: In the pacific, in Europe, and on the continents of Africa and Asia, every branch of the air services now forms close partnerships with the other branches of the armed forces. The roles of transport and supply must now be balanced with combat, and the Army Air Force focuses on protecting allied interests on land and across the oceans.

programme.title: Nazi Concentration Camps
programme.desc: This film is the official documentary report compiled from over 80,000 feet of film shot by Allied military photographers in the German concentration camps immediately after liberation. The footage is a camp-by-camp record taken in order to provide lasting objective proof of the horrors the liberators witnessed. Some emphasis is also placed on the humanitarian work done in camps by the liberators.

programme.title: Shackled
programme.desc: Historians call the December 1950 evacuation from Hungnam in North Korea 'The greatest evacuation movement by sea in U.S. military history'.

programme.title: Modern Warfare: The Vietnam War
programme.desc: The Vietnam War was fought for the defense of democracy. Ten long years of vicious combat - including the Tet Offensive and bloodshed at Hue and Saigon - permanently embedded the Vietnam War in the American consciousness.

programme.title: Kuwait
programme.desc: The war really begins from the moment Saddam Hussein, the president of Iraq, launches his troops into Kuwait. These are spearheaded by 100,000 of his republican guard. Supported by helicopter gunships, armored personnel carriers, mobile artillery and tanks.

programme.title: Autopsy of a Mass Murder
programme.desc: On 20 November 1945, the trial of the top brass of the Third Reich, including Göring, opened in Nuremberg, the city where the anti-Jewish laws were drawn up in 1935. One year later, the international military tribunal sentenced 12 of the accused to death, and seven to jail. Some Jewish witnesses testified, and only Hans Frank, the Governor General of Poland, acknowledged the persecution of Jews.

programme.title: The War at Sea
programme.desc: The Navy copes with supply shortages.

programme.title: Hitler's Evil Scientists
programme.desc: It is a word that sends a chill down the spine: 'Ahnenerbe'. This was the name of the research institute set up to prove the scientific foundation of Nazi ideology. Driven by a scientific megalomania, the race for new discoveries led the institution to carry out countless acts of barbarism.

programme.title: The Tide Begins to Turn: October-December 1942
programme.desc: As 1942 drew to a close, the Allies were really beginning to make headway. The British made a crucial breakthrough in North Africa, and the Americans pushed the Japanese out of Burma and New Guinea. In Russia the Germans found themselves surrounded.

programme.title: Facing the Music: January-March 1943
programme.desc: The only option for the German Sixth Army at Stalingrad was surrender, while all across Russia the Red Army consolidated their advantage. Also, as German cities encountered the kind of bombing that Britain faced back in 1940, courtesy of the RAF.

programme.title: Gateway to Victory
programme.desc: The aerial and amphibious assault on the beaches of Normandy and the allied convoys landing on the Normandy beaches. Shows Gens. Eisenhower and Montgomery and Adm. Sir Bertram Ramsey.

programme.title: Desert Shield
programme.desc: With the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait a great confrontation began. A host of forces around the world were deployed against the Iraqi army. This video ordinance program looks at the weapons of operation Desert Shield.

programme.title: We Strike Back
programme.desc: Pearl Harbor day has etched itself in our history. The entire nation was motivated in a fighting fury. We will see the Japanese seize Hong Kong, Singapore, Philippines, and the Dutch East Indies. General McArthur is profiled.

programme.title: Bandits at Three O'clock
programme.desc: The speed of sound had probably been broken before by several Second World War aircraft. Some British and American fighters may have unintentionally exceeded the speed of sound in an evasive dive. In November 1945, a British jet fighter the Gloster Meteor set a new official world speed record of 606.25 mph. Two years later the sound barrier was broken by an American aircraft, the Bell X-1.

programme.title: Beachhead and Breakthrough
programme.desc: Eisenhower inspects the landing beaches and we see the 'Mulberry' harbors put in place along the Normandy beaches. Airfields are built and supplies are offloaded. V-1 rockets attack London. We see the Germans build V-2 rockets. Storms wreck a Mulberry harbor and damage the other. Cherbourg is taken but is wrecked by the Germans. The British and Canadians work to take Caen.

programme.title: Heinrich Himmler
programme.desc: The Occult Roots of the Third Reich. The creator of the infamous Gestapo, the Waffen SS and the concentration camp network. Perhaps the strangest individual of all the Nazi crew. Himmler was inspired by mystic visions, runes, horoscopes and a longing for a heroic German past.

programme.title: Episode 1
programme.desc: In this episode, the pilots of a Soviet aviation regiment face challenges during World War II. They engage in combat, search for a downed German pilot, and receive a new recruit. The episode explores the camaraderie and determination of the pilots in the face of adversity.

programme.title: The Cold War
programme.desc: The Cold War sheds a new light on the clandestine wars fought between the US and the Soviet Union. This documentary takes us across the world in the turbulent 50s, 60s and 70s: an era of spies, secrets and lies. Thanks to recently disclosed images and files from the CIA and Russia's KGB, and with access to rare archive footage, we reveal a clearer picture of what was happening behind the scenes.

programme.title: Vietnam Firefight
programme.desc: In the Vietnam War, flying into jungle produces a different kind of hazard. In a daring rescue mission a desperate pilot cuts his own landing zone in forty foot tall bamboo. They come under heavy fire as they return again and again to pick up more survivors from the bamboo circle.

programme.title: Theater Commanders
programme.desc: Outstanding military Naval leaders, soldiers, sailors, and marines are discussed and the Theater commanders of General Dwight D. Eisenhower are also discussed.

programme.title: Victory
programme.desc: Monash takes up the challenge of vigorous pursuit of the Germans and in one day advance 10 kilometres and takes two and a half thousand prisoners - one week later the war is over.

programme.title: Little Private
programme.desc: Nothing prepares soldiers to be surrounded by enemy tanks and infantry. When tasked with defending a recently captured town in Bastogne, Belgium, Joe's aging platoon awoke to find themselves surrounded, outnumbered and outgunned. His platoon dumbfounded; Private Joseph Richardson took matters into his own hands. Grasping a bazooka Joe sought to break up the German counterattack.

programme.title: 1944 - Ardennes' Battle/Battle of the Bulge
programme.desc: It is in the heart of the Ardennes massif that will take place one of the bloodiest battles of the Second World War. A few days before Christmas, 500,000 Germans are preparing to stampede on the allied forces stationed in the sector. In the early hours of the assault on December 16th, 1944, the American forces are taken by surprise. Discover what actually happened in Ardennes in the winter 1944.

programme.title: Episode 5
programme.desc: Makeev's team rescues Smereko from the chemical test site; he survived with a stolen protective mask and reports mass poisonings, including women and children. Zvonareva urges aerial destruction, but Nenarokov demands firmer proof. Shevchenko proposes a risky low pass over the warm-spring lake to drop scouts into the water without parachutes.

programme.title: Hitler's Eastern Front: Army Group North
programme.desc: As Europe staggered toward war, Stalin saw opportunity to gain territory for Russia and stand apart from imperialist conflict between Britain, France and Germany. He abandoned cooperation from western pals. By agreeing to share polish territory between the 3rd Reich and the Soviet Union after invasion, Hitler kept the Russians at bay on his eastern borders to devote attention to war with the west.

programme.title: Big Picture: The 7th Infantry in Korea
programme.desc: At the end of World War 2 the 7th accepted Japanese surrender in Korea. In 1950 they return to the new war.

programme.title: One Demerit to Go
programme.desc: On the brink of failure, many give up but some fight twice as hard. Establishing a military academy in Munich, the Seventh Army trained non-commissioned officers. One of these students, Sgt. Leon Carroll had, to this point, received twenty demerits. He mobilized all his intelligence and leadership to complete his course avoiding the final demerit which would result in discharge.

programme.title: Episode 8
programme.desc: At an airfield, Ivan, a new recruit, meets Lyudmila, a skilled pilot concealing an ailment. She mentors him as Lenya, the strict trainer, pushes Martynov, a rebellious trainee. When scouts go missing, aerial battles ensue, forging deep bonds, and unveiling secrets. Amidst peril and personal struggles, they find courage, love, and hope.

programme.title: Victory at Last
programme.desc: The victories at Manila and Okinawa are discussed.

programme.title: Bloody Iwo
programme.desc: To help their long-range bombers over Japan, the Allied forces need the island of Iwo Jima, but face strong Japanese resistance on the beach.

programme.title: ManHunt
programme.desc: A drug gang knocks over a DEA evidence warehouse and proves elusive for the members of the team; Antwon has a seizure while chasing down the leader of the gang.

programme.title: Double Trouble
programme.desc: Nash and Joe (Don Johnson, Cheech Marin) find out that someone has been "borrowing" the name of their detective agency. Guest stars: Jenna Lewis, Joel Klug, Sean Kenniff and Gervase Peterson of "Survivor."

programme.title: End Game
programme.desc: Nash and the others uncover a deadly game wherein the players try to assassinate each other; Nash's friend Boz Bishop is framed for murder.

programme.title: Blow Out
programme.desc: Nash and Joe track down former SIU officer Rick Bettina, who escaped during his parole hearing to recover the money he stole.

programme.title: The Messenger
programme.desc: Nash protects a newscaster from a deranged fan; Joe is caught in the middle of a crime while selling his car.

programme.title: Grave Robbers
programme.desc: Nash takes on the case of a clever con man who fakes his own death after ripping off a dangerous organized crime boss; Joe learns that his mother-in-law smokes marijuana.

programme.title: Bear Trap
programme.desc: Nash and Joe bear down on black market poachers selling animal gall bladders; the office buzzes with rumors of a romance between Nash and Rachel.

programme.title: Recover Me
programme.desc: A wealthy accounting adviser sets Rachel up for a murder, and her lack of cooperation confuses Nash until he discovers a secret from her past.

programme.title: Something Borrowed
programme.desc: Nash is flabbergasted to learn that he's legally married to Tamara Van Zant and comes to the conclusion that she's up to her old tricks again; Nick acts as a "beard" for a lesbian friend.

programme.title: Out of Miami
programme.desc: U.S. Marshal Rick Hawks comes back to the Bay Area to transport a key witness in an important drug trafficking case.

programme.title: Slam Dunk!
programme.desc: Nash and Joe investigate the murder of a wealthy lawyer; Cassidy and Rachel are caught in a love triangle.

programme.title: The Partner
programme.desc: Nash and the SIU team try to stop a vigilante who is killing the criminals that are under investigation.

programme.title: Blood Bots
programme.desc: Nash tracks the ringleader of a new technical gang who built a small army of remote-controlled robots, fully equipped with heavy artillery, to pull off a string of robberies.

programme.title: Quack Fever
programme.desc: Painful memories and the dangers of the drug trade collide when Nick learns the truth about Nash's older brother Bobby, who was supposedly missing for more than 20 years.

programme.title: Kill Joy
programme.desc: The murder of a newscaster begins a string of stalkings involving women of the same name, and Harvey eventually discovers the killer's motive.

programme.title: Change Up
programme.desc: Cassidy's future in law enforcement comes under question when her and Rachel's attempts to stop a bank robbery can't prevent an executive's death.

programme.title: Cat Fight
programme.desc: Nash turns up a handful of surprises when tracking down two young women responsible for the death of a security guard during a robbery at a rock concert.

programme.title: Fair Game
programme.desc: While questioning her career in law enforcement, Cassidy steps into the wrong taxi at the wrong time when she becomes a killer cabby's fare; Rachel learns that Nash is being set up.

programme.title: Genesis
programme.desc: A San Francisco police investigator (Don Johnson) uses keen instincts, wit and charm on the job but has less success in his personal life.

programme.title: Home Invasion
programme.desc: A gang terrorizes Nash's (Don Johnson) ex-wife (Serena Scott Thomas) and daughter (Jodi Lyn O'Keefe); Joe (Cheech Marin) moves in.

programme.title: Skirt Chasers
programme.desc: A heroin dealer sets up shop in San Francisco, but his penchant for buying time with women gives Nash and his team a shot at taking him down.

programme.title: High Impact
programme.desc: Nash and Joe Dominguez try to protect the mayor when a religious fanatic takes fire and brimstone seriously and detonates bombs all over San Francisco.

programme.title: The Javelin Catcher
programme.desc: A deadly military weapon stolen by gang members leads Nash to work with a military adviser before more gang violence erupts.

programme.title: Vanishing Act
programme.desc: When a sting operation falls apart and Harvey Leek disappears with the government's money, Joe and Nash set out to prove his innocence.

programme.title: Aloha, Nash
programme.desc: Nash puts his romantic vacation with Kelly on hold to pursue the evils behind an incriminating betting book; Ian's girlfriend is taken hostage.

programme.title: Key Witness
programme.desc: Nash sets out to help Lisa, whose eyewitness account of a murder raises some eyebrows when no body can be found; Joe checks out his new investment.

programme.title: Internal Affairs
programme.desc: Nash must clear his name after being suspended following an Internal Affairs accusation that he murdered a suspect in revenge.

programme.title: Till Death Do Us Part
programme.desc: Joe is exposed to a deadly virus after a thief unwittingly releases it into the air while foraging for drugs at a chemical lab.

programme.title: The Great Escape
programme.desc: Nash's daughter, Cassidy, is kidnapped by an escaped anti-government extremist who is out to avenge his imprisonment and separation from his family.

programme.title: Wrecking Crew
programme.desc: Nash and Joe are taken hostage while attempting to nab a gang of professional thieves during a robbery.

programme.title: Trackdown
programme.desc: Nash attempts to apprehend a former best friend who has become an international mercenary sent to San Francisco for a hit.

programme.title: The Brothers McMillan
programme.desc: Dead bodies begin surfacing as two brothers vie for control of the Irish mafia in San Francisco; Joe suspects someone is stealing from his bar.

programme.title: Night Train
programme.desc: Nash and his team take the subway home from a bachelor party and are held hostage after walking into the midst of a robbery.

programme.title: Zodiac
programme.desc: Nash calls on his former mentor, Dale Cutter, for help in a murder case that has all the signs of the infamous Zodiac killings.

programme.title: Leo's Big Score
programme.desc: Nash baby-sits a juvenile felon marked for death by drug dealers; Joe gives his son J.J. a job at the bar.

programme.title: Hit Parade
programme.desc: A money launderer-turned-informant is killed, and Nash and Joe discover they are next in line unless they can find the hit man first.

programme.title: Promised Land
programme.desc: A student accused of attempted murder leads Nash and Joe to a Chinese slavery ring smuggling illegal immigrants into the country.

programme.title: 25 Hours of Christmas
programme.desc: Christmas is put on hold as Nash and Joe investigate the death of a store executive murdered at the site of a professional jewelry heist.

programme.title: Road Work
programme.desc: An information leak linked to the government endangers the lives of Nash and Joe, and the federal witness they must protect.

programme.title: Inside Out
programme.desc: Joe infiltrates a prison when all the evidence in the murder of an undercover police officer points to an incarcerated drug lord.

programme.title: The Counterfeiters
programme.desc: Nash and Joe discover that a group is impersonating the Special Investigations Unit in order to pull off a $20 million counterfeit heist.

programme.title: The Web
programme.desc: Nash and Joe learn that a hacker is stealing prototype computer equipment to pay the ransom on his kidnapped wife.

programme.title: Knockout
programme.desc: Nash and Joe search for the perpetrators of a series of sex crimes when Nash's sister, Stacy, becomes a victim and can't remember anything about the attack.

programme.title: Gun Play
programme.desc: While Cassidy recuperates after being struck by a stray bullet, Nash and Joe look for both the shooter and the gun supplier.

programme.title: Rampage
programme.desc: Inspector Robbins wants Nash and Joe to track down his teenage daughter who has joined a convicted felon on a crime spree.

programme.title: Out of Chicago
programme.desc: A beautiful Chicago detective helps Nash and Joe investigate a triple murder; Joe calls a hypnotist for a melancholy racehorse.

programme.title: Moving Target
programme.desc: Searching for a criminal puts Nash and Joe in competition with a bounty hunter who used to be Nash's boss.

programme.title: Wild Card
programme.desc: While eluding a Florida gangster, a former partner enlists Nash's help in finding the man who cheated him in a poker game.

programme.title: Deliverance
programme.desc: Nash and Joe learn that drug dealers are being executed by a commando hired to protect an urban community.

programme.title: Lost and Found
programme.desc: An explosive encounter with carjackers puts Nash on their trail and into conflict with a policewoman who believes he's compromised her undercover investigation.

programme.title: Payback

programme.title: Shake, Rattle and Roll
programme.desc: Babysitters Nash and Joe must stop a hit man; Nick has an unsuitable love interest (Jennifer O'Neill).

programme.title: One Flew Over the 'Cuda's Nest
programme.desc: An escaped mental patient goes on a literary killing spree; Joe and Inger regret hiring Nash's baby-nurse friend.

programme.title: Blackout
programme.desc: Nash (Don Johnson) finds a murder case much more difficult to crack after a bomb blast gives him amnesia. With Cheech Marin.

programme.title: Ripcord
programme.desc: A burglar escapes by leaping from the 35th floor with a parachute; Nick volunteers for an experimental program at the university.

programme.title: Sniper
programme.desc: Nash and Joe track a sniper in San Francisco; a social club celebrates Halloween daily; guest Cassandra Peterson, "Elvira."

programme.title: Revelations
programme.desc: A clash between rival drug lords uncovers new evidence on the whereabouts of Nash's missing brother, presumed killed in the Vietnam War.

programme.title: Most Wanted
programme.desc: A convict inadvertently released by county officers targets Michelle; a TV reporter is being blackmailed.

programme.title: Bombshell

programme.title: Jamie's Show-Stopping Christmas Porchetta

As the brutal murders continue, worried residents start to prepare for a final showdown that pits neighbor against neighbor.

programme.title: The Tax Collector
programme.desc: Two enforcers for a crime lord face an uncertain future when an old rival reappears.

programme.title: White Elephant

With an eager underling out to prove himself, rival gangs making moves, and a rising body count, every step Tancredi makes threatens lives -- including his own.

programme.title: Dog Eat Dog
programme.desc: Ex-cons, Troy (Nicolas Cage), Mad Dog (Willem Dafoe) and Diesel (Christopher Matthew Cook), are hired by an eccentric mob boss to kidnap a baby and hold it for a large ransom. When the abduction goes awry, the men find themselves on the run from the mob and the cops. Vowing to stay out of prison at all costs, getting away with the crime is a matter of life and death.

programme.title: Clean
programme.desc: A tormented garbage man named Clean tries to live a quiet life of redemption, but when his good intentions make him the target of a local crime boss, he must soon reconcile with the violence of his past.

programme.desc: An impending deadline leaves the firm in disarray; Don makes Peggy stay late to work on a Samsonite ad, missing a birthday dinner with her boyfriend, Mark.

programme.title: The Summer Man
programme.desc: Don attempts to regain control over his life through physical changes and journal writing; Don's persistence with Faye results in an impromptu dinner date.

programme.title: Beirut
programme.desc: Anthony travels to "The Paris of the Middle East" known as Beirut; a city well known for its incredible cuisine and infamous nightlife.

programme.title: Naples and the Amalfi Coast
programme.desc: Feasting on pizza in Naples; finding the freshest mozzarella and the best San Marzano tomatoes; enjoying spaghetti and zucchini.

programme.title: Rome
programme.desc: Stanley heads to Rome in search of the famous four pastas, orders rigatoni all'amatriciana, samples carbonara and tries a selection of cheeses and sausages made from the sheep and pigs farmed in the region.

programme.title: Bologna
programme.desc: Stanley Tucci explores Bologna, seen by many as the food capital of Italy; the region of Emilia-Romagna is home to globally renowned protected food products.

programme.title: Milan
programme.desc: In Milan, Stanley enjoys an aperitivo and makes pizzoccheri; classic Milanese veal chops and risotto.

programme.title: Tuscany
programme.desc: Stanley explores his former home of Tuscany; he participates in a wine bar crawl, celebrates the importance of the lowly loaf and samples dishes which use stale bread as the key ingredient.

programme.title: Sicily
programme.desc: In Sicily, Stanley tastes the grapes grown in the region's unique soils and reflects on Sicilian hospitality.

programme.title: Punjab
programme.desc: Anthony dives into the ever-changing state of Punjab with a trip to Amritsar, sampling cuisine at a roadside restaurant, a Sikh celebration and a free community vegetarian restaurant.

programme.title: Las Vegas
programme.desc: Anthony pals up with food author Michael Ruhlman as they visit the Huntridge Tavern and Jose Andres' restaurant é; Penn Jillette and former mayor Oscar Goodman are pokin' around.

programme.title: Lyon
programme.desc: Anthony and Daniel Boulud travel to Lyon, France, to visit the city's rich food culture and legendary chefs.

programme.title: Mexico
programme.desc: Anthony travels to Mexico City, Oaxaca, and Cuernavaca to talk with local residents who express their passion through food and later to journalist Anabel Hernandez on the drug trade-related violence's impact.

programme.title: Mississippi
programme.desc: Anthony explores Mississippi including the home of the "Pig Ear Sandwich," downtown Jackson's Big Apple Inn, also known as a Civil Rights Era gathering place; then on to an old sharecropper structure turned juke joint, Po' Monkey's Social Club.

programme.title: Thailand
programme.desc: Anthony treks to the Chiang Mai province of Northern Thailand where he catches up with celebrated chef Andy Ricker of Pok Pok restaurants fame to explore the country's diverse and various seasonal eating and drinking scene.

programme.title: Brazil
programme.desc: Visiting Bahia, the African heart of Brazil; the dance/martial art of Capoeira; legendary food vendors; Salvadoran fishing neighborhoods.

programme.title: The Takeover
programme.desc: In under two centuries, favorite food brands span continents and cultures, spur innovation and technology, and forever change the food landscape.

programme.title: The Taste
programme.desc: Food preferences are influenced by dozens of factors, including genetics, environment and habit, but the taste is also about perception; the color, texture and weight of food are as important as the flavor.

programme.title: The Marketing
programme.desc: At one point, each and every food brand had to come up with a plan to get people to try them; today, the food and drink marketing industry is worth about $900 billion and growing.

programme.title: The Supply Chain
programme.desc: With every single bite or sip that people take, they participate in one of the most sophisticated journeys around the world ever taken; the global food supply chain is part of an $8 trillion network that produces over 4 billion tons of food annually.

programme.title: The Impact
programme.desc: Food brands travel around the world, stick around and change the places they visit; once the food is adopted by eager taste buds, it becomes part of local culture and tradition.

programme.title: The Future
programme.desc: Climate change, a global pandemic, and a booming world population mark an opportune time to be in the food business, not unlike the first wave of the industrial food revolution that gave people the first globally mass-produced, processed foods.

programme.desc: María decide provocar un encuentro con Albertano para verlo directamente a los ojos y descubrir si es el amor de su vida. La vida de Albertano corre peligro y María se arriesga para salvarlo.

programme.title: El loco corte de pelo
programme.desc: Con la reunión de exalumnos de Federica a la vuelta de la esquina, ella se siente algo insegura por su apariencia. Entonces decide hacerse un arriesgado cambio de look.

programme.title: El genio bursátil
programme.desc: Ludovico se mete en problemas en el trabajo cuando trata de ayudar a Don Camerino en asuntos financieros. Tratando de resolver el desorden, Ludovico complica todo aún más, pero Junior lo ayudará a salir del problema.

programme.title: El crimen del padre Memo
programme.desc: Es la tan esperada boda entre Toña y Brayan, pero Rocío le pide al padre Memo que sea él quien los case.

programme.desc: Paco y Chío se despiden de Fran, quien vuelve a Estados Unidos. Paco tiene miedo de la soledad y toma una decisión que sorprende a todos.

programme.title: Volver al futuro
programme.desc: Los vecinos se quedan sin agua porque Germán no pagó el servicio. Además, tienen que arreglar algunas fugas de agua, pero Germán los convence de que mejor se compren una mesa de tenis de mesa.

programme.title: Intercambio escolar
programme.desc: Marco le pedirá a Alejandra que le falsifique su boleta a cambio de dinero. Magdalena al ver la boleta de su hijo, estará orgullosa y pensará en mandarlo a una de las mejores escuelas del país.

programme.title: Un héroe chapín

programme.title: Motociclistas

programme.title: Día del niño

programme.title: Abuelo astuto
programme.desc: Don Arnoldo puede morir en cualquier momento y la familia López lo complace en todo lo que quiera. Pero el abuelo se entera de que su diagnóstico fue erróneo y no está dispuesto a renunciar a todas las atenciones que recibe.

programme.title: Cuando llegó el abuelo

programme.title: Welcome to ELEI
programme.desc: Los héroes llegan a Los Ángeles y piensan que su presentación va a ser en el estadio de los Dodgers. En realidad, son los invitados especiales del aniversario del mercado de East LA.

programme.title: La boda de mi mejor amigo
programme.desc: Vítor ha encontrado a la mujer de su vida y decide casarse con ella, pero Albertano hace todo por impedir esa boda, tras descubrir que ella es una peligrosa criminal.

programme.title: Sin dinero
programme.desc: Vítor y Albertano se dan cuenta de que se han gastado todo su dinero. Ahora tienen que pedirle comida prestada a sus vecinos para poder sobrevivir.

programme.title: El papá de la nena
programme.desc: Los López preparan una fiesta sorpresa para La Nena. Carlos, el papá de La Nena reaparece inesperadamente y le cuenta cómo ha sido su vida.

programme.title: Martina y Ricky
programme.desc: Martina tiene su primer novio, pero las cosas se salen de control cuando se inventa una vida que no tiene y a su vez, él también tiene un secreto que no se imaginan.

programme.title: Cambio de cuerpos
programme.desc: Al tratar de arreglar la antena de la televisión, un rayo cae sobre los López, provocando que todos cambien de personalidad. Renata le pide ayuda a una curandera y Plácido descubre que todo era un sueño.

programme.title: Cambio de hábitos
programme.desc: A Renata se le ocurre desintoxicar a su familia, así que les informa que cambiarán sus hábitos alimenticios. Don Arnoldo escucha que La Nena ya tiene novio y aprovecha para chantajearla con comida.

programme.title: Los chiles de la discordia
programme.desc: Carmelo queda encerrado probando la alarma del negocio. María sueña que debe ganarse el corazón de Doña Lucha para conquistar a Albertano, y para eso prepara unos deliciosos chiles, aunque esto despierta un sentimiento de competencia.

programme.title: San Chambelán
programme.desc: María quiere celebrar su fiesta de quince años, pero para eso utiliza dinero que no es suyo. Doña Lucha entrena al Chino para ser chambelán. Albertano se ofrece a ser el chambelán de María.

programme.title: La Navidad perfecta
programme.desc: Ludovico sufre un infarto y muere. Santa Ninel le pide cambiar su forma de ser para antes de Navidad si no quiere morir. Ludovico hace todo por cambiar con su familia.

programme.title: Recuerdos
programme.desc: Ludovico habla de su familia: cuando conoció a Federica, cuando se enteró de que iba a ser padre y de otros graciosos momentos que han marcado su vida.

programme.title: Hijo de tigre pintito
programme.desc: Paco recibe la visita de una ex quien le deja una bendición del pasado: se trata de Lucas, un hijo que él no sabía que tenía y que se queda a vivir en su casa a pesar de las protestas de Rocío.

programme.title: El niño espurio
programme.desc: Después de que Toña hace cuentas, Rocío descubre que Lucas es producto de una infidelidad porque aún andaba con Paco, así que le pide una prueba de paternidad para verificar que son padre e hijo.

programme.title: Fantasmas del más acá
programme.desc: Los vecinos están molestos por escuchar ruidos en el edificio y creen que existe un fantasma. Silvia visita al Doctor Cupido y le dará opciones para que encuentre una pareja.

programme.title: Video descompuesta
